items.quote: This policy articulates the duty and commitment of Douglas College (the College) to support students and other members of the College Community who are affected by Sexual Violence or Sexual Misconduct; to create and make available programs and resources to educate students and other members of its Community on the prevention of Sexual Violence and Misconduct; and to provide a fair and effective process for responding to and investigating allegations of Sexual Violence and Misconduct.
items.reason: The policy is a dedicated sexual violence policy with its own independent reporting, investigation, and appeal procedures.
The policy does not commit to posting the policy itself publicly or on the website.

items.quote: A student or any other member of the College Community who has experienced Sexual Violence or Sexual Misconduct, or who is otherwise affected by a violation of this policy, may file a Complaint under this policy with the Director, SSRM.
items.reason: The policy sets out clear steps to report, including who to contact (Director, SSRM), how (in writing), and what happens next (initial review within two business days).

items.quote: which includes but is not limited to protecting the Complainant from unreasonable and/or irrelevant questions, such as those pertaining to past sexual history or gender expression, complying with collective agreement provisions where applicable, and providing regular updates on the status of the process.
items.reason: The protection against questions about past sexual history is limited to those deemed "unreasonable and/or irrelevant."

items.quote: The Investigator will conduct the investigation using a procedurally fair and sensitive process, taking care to minimize or avoid circumstances that might reasonably be expected to cause participants distress (e.g., the Complainant having to come into direct contact with the Respondent).
items.reason: The protection from face-to-face contact is not guaranteed, as the investigator is only required to "take care to minimize or avoid" such circumstances.

items.quote: However, this section does not prevent a. any participants in an investigation from disclosing information about themselves or from disclosing information that they have obtained outside the investigation; or b. College representatives from disclosing investigation-related information as authorized under this policy.
items.reason: The policy explicitly states that participants are not prevented from disclosing information about themselves, meaning they are free to speak about their own experience.

items.quote: A student or any other member of the College Community has the right to pursue other processes external to the College in connection with alleged incidents of Sexual Violence and Misconduct, such as reporting the matter to the police, initiating a civil action, or filing a complaint under the BC Human Rights Code.
items.reason: The right to choose external processes is hedged by the institution's override to report to the police without consent if safety is at risk.

items.quote: A student or other Community member acting in good faith in making a Disclosure or reporting an incident of Sexual Violence or Sexual Misconduct will not be investigated by the College for consuming alcohol or drugs at the time of the disclosed or reported incident(s), even if they were under the legal age for such consumption or the substance was illegal.
items.reason: The policy commits in binding language that a student reporting sexual violence will not be investigated or disciplined for drug or alcohol use at the time of the incident.

items.quote: Except in exceptional circumstances, investigations (including the preparation of the Investigator’s report) will be completed within sixty (60) calendar days of an Investigator’s receipt of a Complaint.
items.reason: The timeline for completing investigations is 60 days, which is slower than the 45-day benchmark, and contains permissive exceptions.

items.quote: The College reserves the right to implement immediate interim measures as it considers appropriate to protect the safety of the College Community or any of its members during an evaluation of a Disclosure or Complaint or pending the completion of an investigation.
items.reason: Interim measures are discretionary, as the policy states the College "reserves the right" to implement them and that they "may include" the listed options.

items.reason: The scope of the policy explicitly and bindingly covers off-campus activities required for studies, specifically naming practicum placements.

items.quote: the Complainant and the Respondent will be notified of the Investigator’s findings and the Respondent will be notified of the Responsible Administrator’s decision regarding disciplinary or other measures to be taken against the Respondent; and
items.reason: The policy only guarantees that the complainant will be notified of the investigator's findings, while notification of disciplinary measures is restricted to the respondent.

items.quote: preparation of statistical reports of Disclosures and Complaints of Sexual Violence and Misconduct made under this policy, as required by and in accordance with applicable legislation; and
items.reason: The policy mentions preparing statistical reports as required by legislation, but does not explicitly commit to publishing them publicly or annually.

items.quote: regular reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of this policy, occurring at least once every three (3) years or as advised by the Minister responsible for advanced education.
items.reason: The policy requires review at least once every three years, which is longer than the two-year benchmark.
The policy does not address student representation on policy review committees.

items.quote: When the College appoints an Investigator to conduct an investigation into a Complaint, consideration will be given to the subject matter of the Complaint and the expertise and training of the Investigator.
items.reason: Training for investigators is mentioned as a consideration rather than a mandatory requirement, and trauma-informed training is not specified.

items.reason: The institution commits in binding language to establishing a program that provides education and training for students.
